anya: quick follow-up to the packaging RFC \/ focusing on a pragmatic local-registry prune playbook for air-gapped sites. want quick :eyes: and any red flags.

kyle: thanks. tell us the failure modes you care about.

anya: two primary failure modes: 1) race between concurrent prune controllers leading to deletion of blobs still referenced by running pods, 2) operator crash during GC that leaves partial state/tombstones which look deleted but aren't fully cleaned or recoverable. both can cause pod restarts to fail in air-gapped installs.

maria: plus we've observed that large blob deletes spike disk IO and can push nodes into pressure, so we need throttling + chunked deletes.

anya: proposed minimal pattern: operator-managed cluster lease + three-phase prune (candidate/dry-run -> tombstone -> chunked-delete) + per-namespace tombstone hold window. flow sketch:
```
1) operator attempts to acquire cluster-scoped CRD lease: prune-lock.<site>
2) enumerate prune candidates (untagged manifests, older than configurable TTL)
3) annotate candidates with `prune.redwood.io/candidate=true` and emit a prune-preview
4) wait dry-run window (default 15m) to collect references and ack from optional node agents
5) transition candidates to `prune.redwood.io/tombstone=true` (retained for tombstone-retain default 24h)
6) background chunked blob delete (chunk-size default 500 blobs, rate-limit default 10/s)
7) on success remove tombstone markers
```

devon: how do we ensure single-writer semantics for the lease? what if the operator OOMs after acquiring it?

anya: implement lease as a CRD object with ownerRef + heartbeat timestamp. operator updates heartbeat every N seconds. on startup, if heartbeat age > lease_grace, operator can force-claim the lease after a short fencing check. also tombstone semantics provide safety: items in tombstone remain accessible to restore until tombstone-retain expires.

kyle: defaults will vary across customers, but we should ship safe defaults: lease_grace=90s, heartbeat_interval=20s, dry-run=15m, tombstone-retain=24h. expose as operator config and console-level overrides.

maria: regarding references: in addition to Kube API scans (imagePullSecrets, pod.Spec.imageIDs), we should offer an optional lightweight node-side agent (registry-prober) that reports in-use blob hashes. keep it optional for air-gapped installs that prefer minimal agents.

anya: agreed. design: node agent posts attestations to the operator via a signed file or CRD status field. operator merges attestations during dry-run before transition to tombstone.

registry-bot: prune-preview job scheduled by operator for site=harbinger at 2026-03-22T15:48Z

devon: naming: use annotation namespace `prune.redwood.io/` for candidate/tombstone fields and CRD name `prune-lock.redwood.io`. also store a `last_deleted_hash` checkpoint on the CRD so deletes can resume mid-chunk if operator changes.

anya: checkpointing noted. partial-delete recovery will resume from last_deleted_hash, marking progress and avoiding duplicated deletes.

kyle: console UX needs to show preview results plus an estimated reclaim size and impacted repositories. important for site ops to validate before commit.

maria: yes, add a `prune-preview` API endpoint the operator serves that returns exact manifest list, blobs per manifest, and estimated bytes reclaimed. wire this into the console as a preview modal.

anya: ops CLI: `redwoodctl registry prune --site <id> --commit` should call preview, show summary, then perform commit with an optional `--dry-run` and `--force`. include `rehydrate` subcommand to re-mark tombstones as protected from a local image snapshot for emergency rollback.

devon: tests: stress harness scenario: 10k manifests, variable tag churn, simulate node churn and operator kill during commit; run without node-agent. acceptance criteria: no failed pod image pulls, no unrecoverable missing blobs, and operator resumes delete with checkpoint.

anya: action items:
- anya: draft short RFC with CRD schema + sample operator flow + kubectl snippets (due Tue)
- kyle: propose heartbeat/grace defaults + autosize heuristics for operator controllers
- maria: design prune-preview API contract + console mockups + rollback UX
- devon: prototype stress harness and checkpoint resume plan

maria: small ask 12: include a quick runbook describing emergency rollback steps (rehydrate tombstones from snapshot, tip to support team). will reduce TTR for onprem incidents.

anya: adding runbook steps to RFC and a `redwoodctl restore` example.

kyle: :thumbsup: sounds like a practical, low-risk incremental feature. this should markedly reduce onprem blast radius.

registry-bot: prune-preview completed (dry-run) site=harbinger candidate_count=412 estimated_reclaim=58GB

devon: great. i'll queue the harness once RFC lands.

anya: thanks everyone. i'll post the RFC link in this channel when it's ready and tag reviewers. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
